entry.title: Marvel Rivals says ‘Klyntar is about to ignite,’ so it seems a season 3 announcement is imminent
entry.summary:
The hype levels for Marvel Rivals' new season are officially reaching critical mass, as NetEase Games has begun to tease the impending arrival of new content once more.
A short teaser video posted on Twitter/X shows what looks like a new section of Klyntar, the symbiote home world and planet led by the god of symbiotes, Knull. In it, there also appears to be a resurrection pod similar to Adam Warlock's ultimate. And inside? We can take an educated guess.
It's most likely Phoenix, AKA X-Men member Jean Grey, who's been leaked before as the season's new hero, along with the vampire slayer Blade, who finally woke up from his months-long nap after being rescued from Dracula's grasp in season one.
Twitch accidentally spilled the beans this past Friday that Phoenix and Blade are coming as new heroes in a blog about upcoming Twitch Drops, but season two's in-game lore has been hinting at Phoenix coming to do battle with Knull for some time.
The symbiote god somehow managed to survive the heroes' previous assault on Klyntar, leading them to enlist the help of "one of the primal forces of the universe" to deal with him, hinting at Jean Grey and her Phoenix alter ego, possessed by the all-powerful Phoenix Force.
Previous leaks hint that both new heroes are likely to be Duelists, but we won't know for sure until there's some official confirmation from NetEase. Considering the new season is now less than two weeks away, we should be getting some news about season three in the coming days to confirm what we already know, and some of what we may not.
The Twitch blog also mentioned "all-new team-ups, stunning Venomized costumes, and sizzling summer events that will turn up the heat," so the latest season of the hero shooter will have a lot of eyes on it when it drops.
Season three of Marvel Rivals will begin on July 11 for PS5, Xbox Series X|S, and PC.

entry.title: How to equip Layered Weapons in Monster Hunter Wilds
entry.summary:
The addition of Layered Weapons in Monster Hunter Wilds adds a new sense of fashion to the endgame, as you can now personalize those beloved blades (or other gear) to look different.
Capcom has finally introduced Layered Weapons to the latest Monster Hunter title. Thanks to this update, you can now make your weapon match the looks of your armor sets. Let's find out how to equip and use Layered Weapons.
Table of contents How to get Layered Weapons in Monster Hunter Wilds How to use Layered Weapons in Monster Hunter Wilds
How to get Layered Weapons in Monster Hunter Wilds
The first task is to craft a Layered Weapon, which can be done with any standard weapon that you made. However, it will take some time and resources, since your weapon will need to be at the highest rarity. The highest rarity will vary with your weapon, but it's safe to assume that you should already have something eligible if you're in the endgame.
Screenshot via Capcom
If you have an Artian Weapon, you can use that as a Layered Weapon. In case of an Artian Weapon, you'll have to refine it all the way up to its highest level before you can turn it into a Layered Weapon. Of course, you will need to make sure to update your game to the latest version to access Title Update 2.
How to use Layered Weapons in Monster Hunter Wilds
To turn an eligible weapon into a layered weapon, you'll need to follow these steps.
Go to the tent
Go to the Appearance Tab.
Select Change Equipment Appearance.
Select your equipped weapons, and it will open the Layered Weapons options (if your weapon meets the requirements).
Once confirmed, your weapons will have a different appearance. Do note that the changes are purely cosmetic.

entry.title: USN-7582-2: Samba regression
entry.summary:
USN-7582-1 fixed vulnerabilities in Samba. The update introduced a regression. This update fixes the problem.
We apologize for the inconvenience.
Original advisory details:
Evgeny Legerov discovered that Samba incorrectly handled buffers in certain GSSAPI routines of Heimdal. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to cause Samba to crash, resulting in a denial of service. (CVE-2022-3437)
Greg Hudson discovered that Samba incorrectly handled PAC parsing. On 32-bit systems, a remote attacker could use this issue to escalate privileges, or possibly execute arbitrary code. (CVE-2022-42898)
Joseph Sutton discovered that Samba could be forced to issue rc4-hmac encrypted Kerberos tickets. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to escalate privileges. This issue only affected Ubuntu 20.04 LTS and Ubuntu 22.04 LTS. (CVE-2022-45141)
Florent Saudel discovered that Samba incorrectly handled certain Spotlight requests. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to cause Samba to consume resources, leading to a denial of service. (CVE-2023-34966)

entry.title: Virtuální Bastlírna vol. LII: Žhavé léto se žhavými technologiemi
entry.summary:
Přemýšlíte, jak začít prázdniny? Už v úterý 1. července se bude konat Virtuální Bastlírna, tedy online setkání bastlířů, techniků, vědců i akademiků, kde se ve volné diskuzi probírají novinky ze světa techniky, ale i jiných zajímavých témat.
Za poslední měsíc jsme byli svědky plamenů několika raket. Zatímco malá raketa od Hondy se úspěšně vznesla a opět přistála, raketa od SpaceX se rozhodla letět všemi směry najednou. Díkybohu méně bombastické je nahlédnutí do jaderných výzkumů odehrávajících se v Řeži, kam se brzy můžete sami podívat. V ČR vznikla první open-source SLS 3D tiskárna a Linux začleňuje do kernelu podporu GPIB.
Za hardware je tu Pro verze HackRF, průhledné plošňáky od JLC PCB nebo open-source e-ink informační panel. Za software tentokrát snad jen obtíže KiCADu se současným stavem Waylandu a přechodu mnoha distribucí na něj. A jako vždy dojde i na bizarnější záležitosti, třeba flexibilní nebo barevné Arduino.
Příští Virtuální Bastlírna se pod taktovkou projektu MacGyver studentského klubu SiliconHill bude konat v úterý 1. července od 20:00 minimálně do 22:00 (ale obvykle končí o dost později). Odkaz na konferenci se před samotnou akcí objeví na bastlířské wiki.

entry.title: The PowerWash clean ‘em up genre is dead, long live the sci-fi undertaker sim
entry.summary:
You'd think there'd be more video games that are explicitly about clearing away corpses, given how many corpses players produce. Getting rid of bodies is a routine problem for developers, with a variety of crafty or cursory solutions. Horror projects such as Resident Evil sometimes resort to accelerated decomposition, with felled zombies dissolving to maggots in seconds, but in most shooters, it's a question of despawning the victims when you look away. Stealth sims mandate a certain level of respectfulness, albeit by accident: stray cadavers must be carefully interred in random dumpsters or closets before they trigger an alarm. As with a lot of things in games, there are technological concerns here that form a curious warping of practicalities in the world beyond the vidbox. Dead bodies in games absorb computing resources that are needed for the next enemies along. Bodies of actual flesh and bone are a weight, if not a burden upon the dead person's loved ones. The memory has to be freed up, so that it can be used for something else.

entry.title: Cyber Knights: Flashpoint review
entry.summary: Cyber Knights: Flashpoint has some excellent nonsense scenario writing propping up mission design. In one early excursion, you remote activate 'defector tech' to convert an enemy agent over to your side, then have a turn to neutralise the neuro-toxin killswitch in their brain with injectors. The game is awash with this sort of campy, techy gangslang. My absolute favourite of these so far is 'chumbo' - apparently a much stupider, funnier, and therefore much better version of 2077's 'choomba'. Similarly, Cyber Knights' script is pure cyberpunk American cheese singles; reliably tropey and enjoyably naff. And yet, I have spent the last week or so popcorn-bucket-deep in the game's drama. There's little as gripping as a good heist; the planning and personalities and stakes, the fated fumbles and slick improvisations. And, once it gets going, CK:F's grip is augmented. Hour one: "lol, chumbo". Hour three: "We've been made, chumbos! Go loud!". Read more

To test this game, you'll need the original version of the game (either from the original hybrid DOS/Windows/Mac CDs or from GOG.com) and a daily development build of ScummVM.
